name: JVM bytecode and class file format
summary: The stack-based instruction set and binary class-file format of the Java Virtual Machine, verified at load time and executed by interpreters and JIT compilers; the compilation target of Java, Kotlin, Scala, Clojure, Groovy and many other languages.
standards: The Java Virtual Machine Specification, Java SE 25 Edition

level_notes.1: The JVMS (one edition per Java SE release) is normative and implementation-independent; JEPs/JSRs record evolution. The verifier's type-checking rules are given in Prolog in JVMS 4.10.1; mechanised semantics exist in Isabelle (Jinja) and Leroy's verification survey.
level_notes.0: HotSpot in openjdk/jdk is the reference implementation (other JVMs: OpenJ9, GraalVM). There is no official textual assembly syntax; Jasmin, asmtools jasm and Krakatau define community assembler syntaxes, and javap prints a de-facto disassembly format.
